text: Come in, sit down. The tea is still hot. My samovar is the only thing in the whole Ford that has never once gone out.
Every evening I set out cups for everyone. No one comes. I set them out anyway. Habit — or hope, I don't know which.

first2.text: You're heading for the beacon, I can see it in your eyes. You won't get far without oil. I don't have much, but I trade. If you find anything worth something by the roads and fences — bring it. I'll give oil, bread or herbs.

hello.text: Sit down, lamplighter. Your cup is waiting.

alt.text: Do you hear? The neighbours are talking again. Three people came in today — just like that, for tea. Sit down, lamplighter, your cup is waiting.

nothing.text: Look along the road to the beacon, by the old fences, by the cart. People dropped a lot when they stopped leaving their homes. Things wait too, just like us.

about.text: On market days you couldn't push your way through to the well. Lia wasn't born yet. She's seven — and all seven years it's been dark. She thinks that's how it should be. That's the most frightening thing of all.

bye.text: Go. And come back — the tea will cool, and I'll brew a fresh pot.

trade_pick.text: Well now, what have you got?

got_oil.text: Here. Oil isn't water — pour it sparingly. Fire likes being cared for.

got_wire.text: Take the copper to Borta, he's been sighing over it for ages. Just don't tell him it's from me — he'll get proud.

got_bread.text: Still warm from the oven. Bread on the road is like a friend: it says nothing, but things are easier with it.

got_herbs.text: Mint and thyme. Brew them by a campfire — you'll remember my teahouse.

text: Lamplighter, wait. I baked a flatbread — an extra one, as if my hands did it on their own.
In the Mire, past the boardwalks, lives Korney the ferryman. He hasn't come to us in twenty years. Proud, or ashamed — I don't know. But bread is bread, even for a proud man. Will you take it?

bread_say.text: Say nothing. Say it's from Mara. He'll understand. And if he doesn't — he'll eat it, and that's good too.

bread_ok.text: I wrapped it in a cloth, two layers. Let him keep the cloth — I bet he doesn't even have one.

text: A letter? For me? This handwriting… It's Timur, my little brother. He left for the city when I still wore braids.
"Sister, all is well with me. I married, and named my daughter Mara — after you. As soon as it gets lighter, we'll come to the Ford for tea. Keep the samovar hot."
I've kept it hot for twenty years, Timur. Twenty years… Lamplighter, here's oil for you. No, don't argue. For news like this — it's too little.
